I looked at both logs from start to finish, with no filters. BGL runs from 3 June 2005 to 4 January 2006, in Los Angeles time (UTC−7, or UTC−8 in winter). OpenStack runs from 14 to 17 May 2017, in UTC. Neither log has data before its first day, so no change can be measured against an earlier period of equal length. I compared the two halves of BGL instead: 3 Jun–18 Sep against 19 Sep–4 Jan.

**One caveat first:** the team names come from a placeholder ownership table that ships with the tool. They are fictional, not your real org chart [Q24].

## Short answer

- **No problem recurs in both systems.** BGL and OpenStack are different systems, logged 12 years apart, with different components and teams [Q24].
- **BGL has almost all of the serious volume:** 855,501 FATAL entries [Q24], 626,756 from the kernel (Node OS) and 228,536 from applications (HPC Applications) [Q53].
- **OpenStack is mostly quiet:** 3,118 WARNING, 10 ERROR and 2 CRITICAL entries out of 207,636 [Q24].

## What keeps recurring (warning and worse, most severe first)

All counts are exact unless marked ≈. "Days present" counts whole days that have any log data.

| # | Problem | Entries | Level | Days present | Over time | Component · team |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Application connection cut** ("link has been severed") [T22] | 26,546 [Q66] | FATAL | 35 of 213 [Q66] | None in Jun–Sep; all 26,546 in Sep–Jan, on 35 of 107 days [Q72] | APP · HPC Applications, 1,024 nodes [Q66] |
| 2 | **Program image won't load: permission denied** [T16] | 43,040 [Q66] | FATAL | 27 of 213 [Q66] | 3,360 in the first half, 39,680 in the second [Q72] | APP · HPC Applications, 1,024 nodes [Q66] |
| 3 | **Data TLB error interrupt** [T6] | 152,734 [Q66] | FATAL | 11 of 213 [Q66] | 152,723 in the first half, 11 in the second [Q72] | KERNEL · Node OS. **152,182 of the entries come from one node, R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01** [Q73] |
| 4 | **Kernel "instruction address" reports** (crash detail lines) [T13] | 47,563 FATAL [Q66], 51,227 at all levels [Q73] | FATAL | **145 of 213, the most persistent** [Q66] | 51,049 in the first half, 178 in the second, but still on 71 of 107 days [Q72] | KERNEL · Node OS, about 23,000 nodes, at most 12 entries on any one node [Q66][Q73] |
| 5 | **Program image won't load: file missing** [T14] | 46,416 [Q66] | FATAL | 67 of 213 [Q66] | 15,536 in the first half, 30,880 in the second [Q72] | APP · HPC Applications, 1,024 nodes [Q66] |
| 6 | **Login failed: working directory missing** [T15] | 43,647 [Q66] | FATAL | 37 of 213 [Q66] | About level: 22,224 then 21,423 [Q72] | APP · HPC Applications [Q66] |
| 7 | **Lustre file-system mount failed** [T21] | 26,426 [Q66] | FATAL | 12 of 213 [Q66] | All in the first half, mostly late in it; none since 19 Sep [Q72] | KERNEL · Node OS, 1,024 nodes [Q66] |
| 8 | **Data storage interrupt** [T12] | 63,491 [Q66] | FATAL | 5 of 213 [Q66] | 63,490 in the first half, 3 in the second [Q72] | KERNEL · Node OS [Q66] |
| 9 | **Control-system ASSERT failures** ("idoproxydb hit ASSERT") [T10] | 84,250 [Q73] | ERROR [Q53] | 1 day in the first half, 2 in the second [Q72] | Bursts: 19,320 then 64,930 [Q72] | MMCS · Control System. No node is recorded on these entries [Q73] |
| 10 | **OpenStack: unknown base file in the image cache** [T9] | 3,059 [Q67] | WARNING | 25 of 30 hours [Q67] | 270, 1,966 and 823 entries on 14, 16 and 17 May [Q74] | nova.virt.libvirt.imagecache · Virtualization [Q67] |
| 11 | **OpenStack: image-cache maintenance job crashed** [T45] | 8 [Q67] | ERROR | 8 of 30 hours [Q67] | 6 on 16 May, 2 on 17 May [Q74] | oslo_service.periodic_task · Compute Service [Q67] |
| 12 | **OpenStack: login token check failed** [T48] | 2 [Q67] | CRITICAL | 2 of 30 hours [Q67] | 1 each on 16 and 17 May [Q74] | keystonemiddleware.auth_token · Identity & Access [Q67] |

## What to investigate first

The tool's own ranking puts the kernel "instruction address" reports [T13] first, with a score of 14 out of 18 [Q66]. It scores highest because it appears on the most days and is spread over the most nodes. **I'd pick differently.** In the second half it dropped to 178 entries [Q72], so most of its volume belongs to the past. These three look more useful to start with:

1. **The application connection cut [T22] → HPC Applications.** It is the only leading problem that was absent in the first 108 days and then appeared on 35 of the next 107 days, on 1,024 nodes [Q72][Q66]. The two program-load failures with the same owner, "permission denied" [T16] and "file missing" [T14], are also higher in the second half [Q72].
   - Hypothesis: the 1,024 nodes are the machine's I/O nodes, and one cause such as a job launcher or file server is behind all three.
2. **Data TLB errors [T6] → Node OS (possibly together with Hardware Reliability).** 152,182 of the 152,734 entries come from one node, R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 [Q73]. Because it is concentrated on one node, it is the cheapest to check.
   - Hypothesis: a faulty node or memory part.
3. **Control-system ASSERT bursts [T10] → Control System.** 84,250 entries in a few bursts, with the later burst the larger: 19,320 then 64,930 [Q73][Q72].

**For OpenStack,** the only ongoing signal is the image-cache warning [T9], present in 25 of 30 hours [Q67]. Virtualization should check whether it is related to the 8 crashes of the image-cache maintenance job [T45], which Compute Service owns [Q74].
   - Hypothesis: the warning itself is routine housekeeping noise, and the crashes are the part that matters.

## What the counts don't tell you

- **Entries are not incidents.** 152,182 lines from one node may be a single fault that repeated itself. The application errors appearing on exactly 1,024 nodes [Q73] could be a few jobs that each logged once per node.
- **There is no "new" and no percentage change.** Neither log has data before its first day [Q66][Q67]. BGL has no entries on 1 August 2005, and OpenStack none on 15 May 2017 [Q66][Q67]. I compare raw counts only.
- **Causes are hypotheses.** Nothing above about I/O nodes, hardware or housekeeping noise is shown by the logs.
- **Impact isn't measured.** The logs don't show downtime or which users or jobs were affected.
- **Coverage gaps:**
  - The table's "≈" figures are survey estimates from a 100,000-entry random sample, within ±2–10% [Q55][Q56].
  - The ranking considered only the 15 largest of 405 warning-and-worse BGL problem types, so rarer ones weren't ranked [Q66].

- **[Q55]** Survey of BGL message types, all time, 100k random sample. `SELECT regexp_replace(… msg …) … FROM extractor.lt_bgl`
- **[Q56]** Survey of OpenStack message types, all time, 100k random sample. `SELECT regexp_replace(… msg …) … FROM extractor.lt_openstack`
- **[Q66]** Ranking of BGL warning-and-worse problems, 3 Jun 2005 to 5 Jan 2006 (Los Angeles time), exact counts. `SELECT count(*) FROM extractor.lt_bgl WHERE "ts" >= '2005-06-03T07:00:00+00:00' AND "ts" < '2006-01-05T08:00:00+00:00' AND level IN ('ERROR','FAILURE','FATAL','SEVERE','WARNING')`
- **[Q67]** Ranking of OpenStack warning-and-worse problems, 14–18 May 2017 UTC, exact counts. `SELECT count(*) FROM extractor.lt_openstack WHERE "ts" >= '2017-05-14T00:00:00+00:00' AND "ts" < '2017-05-18T00:00:00+00:00' AND level IN ('CRITICAL','ERROR','WARNING')`
- **[Q72]** Daily trend of 10 BGL problems, 19 Sep 2005 to 5 Jan 2006 compared with 3 Jun to 19 Sep 2005 (Los Angeles time), exact. `SELECT bucket, p, comp, k, count(*) AS n FROM (SELECT … CASE WHEN msg LIKE '%interrupt%' … THEN 1 …`
- **[Q73]** Exact counts by node for BGL problems T6, T10, T13, T14 and T104 (T502 was merged into it), all time. `SELECT tpl, k0, count(*) AS n FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN regexp_full_match(… 'data TLB error interrupt' …) THEN 0 …`
- **[Q74]** Exact counts by component and day for OpenStack problems T9, T43, T45 and T48, all time, UTC. `SELECT tpl, k0, k1, count(*) AS n FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN regexp_full_match(… 'Unknown base file:' …) THEN 0 …`
